  "summary": "Bumps the minimum required GCC version from 12.1 to 13.1 and enforces C++20 std::format support at CMake configure time. CI configurations are updated accordingly, including switching the previous-releases test runner to Ubuntu 24.04 and NetBSD cross-compilation to GCC 14 libstdc++. It also converts a benchmark call from tinyformat to std::format as a demonstration.",
  "problem": "Developers cannot use C++20 std::format or prepare the codebase for C++23 because GCC 12 lacks full std::format support. Users on older Linux distributions without GCC 13 or modern Clang will no longer be able to build from source using default distribution packages.",
  "evidence": [
    "PR description: 'For this bump, only C++20 std::format will become available, but this bump should also pave the way for C++23.'",
    "PR description notes target release timing: 'This patch will only be released in version 33.x, or later, next year (2027).'"
  ],

  "card": "PR 36042 raises the minimum supported GCC compiler version from 12.1 to 13.1 and enforces std::format support during CMake configuration. This unblocks the adoption of C++20 std::format and prepares the project for eventual C++23 migration. result.summary: Bumps the minimum required GCC version from 12.1 to 13.1 and enforces C++20 std::format support at CMake configure time. CI configurations are updated accordingly, including switching the previous-releases test runner to Ubuntu 24.04 and NetBSD cross-compilation to GCC 14 libstdc++. It also converts a benchmark call from tinyformat to std::format as a demonstration.
result.problem: Developers cannot use C++20 std::format or prepare the codebase for C++23 because GCC 12 lacks full std::format support. Users on older Linux distributions without GCC 13 or modern Clang will no longer be able to build from source using default distribution packages.
evidence: PR description: 'For this bump, only C++20 std::format will become available, but this bump should also pave the way for C++23.'
PR description notes target release timing: 'This patch will only be released in version 33.x, or later, next year (2027).'
result.scope_notes: Touches CMake feature detection, NetBSD cross-compilation CI packages, Ubuntu CI base images, and documentation across multiple files.
result.changed_since_previous: Drops manual -Werror compiler flags from the native previous releases CI runner in favor of CMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR, and includes minor NetBSD CI adjustments.
result.card: PR 36042 raises the minimum supported GCC compiler version from 12.1 to 13.1 and enforces std::format support during CMake configuration. This unblocks the adoption of C++20 std::format and prepares the project for eventual C++23 migration. CI environments are upgraded to match, including migrating the previous-releases runner to Ubuntu 24.04 and updating NetBSD cross-builds to GCC 14 runtime libraries. Users building on distributions that do not ship GCC 13 by default will need to rely on Clang or third-party toolchains.

risk.why: A broken CMake compiler feature check or toolchain bump could cause build failures for developers and packagers building from source on older platforms.
